_comment: The forms that figure, parallelism and contrast notes in config/figures/ may use. Shown only at Deep.
label is the plain name a reader sees first; term is the usual name for the form; about says what it is in plain words.

defined, where present, is the form defined in the words of a book that defines it: source is an id in config/layer-sources.json (which says who wrote its words), quote its exact words, at where in the book, url the page they are on, read the edition or site the words were read from and retrieved the date (decision 10). Pages of Bullinger's Figures of Speech Used in the Bible (1898) are the printed pages of the archive.org scan figuresofspeechu00bull.

quotable lists the cite-list ids whose words may be shown in a figure note: public-domain works whose words are their named writer's own, in a copy free to quote. Left out, per docs/local-work/2026-10-20/voices/VOICES-SHORTLIST.md as the founder approved it: Gill and Spurgeon (the only typed texts are editors' with rights reserved), the Geneva notes (no free-to-copy statement, and a modern editor's notes mixed in), the Companion Bible (its one typed copy has no license and garbles letters, and it was completed after Bullinger's death in 1913 by others, in parts not yet established), Henry's Concise and Wesley (abridgments, much of them in Henry's, Poole's or Bengel's words), the church fathers (a group, not one work) and the Pulpit Commentary (Bible Hub's text carries BibleSoft's copyright notice; it may be cited and linked, never quoted). The NET translators' notes are never shown. Works left out may still be linked from Layers.

A cite or definition names no writer itself: the cite list in config/layer-sources.json says who wrote a source's words on each book, as it does for Layers (decision 10), so a work by several hands credits each book's own writer, two works by one writer count once toward a note's strength, and words whose writer is not named or is no longer cited are refused.

forms.label: Said twice
forms.about: The second line says the first again in other words.

defined.quote: This is when the lines are parallel in thought, and in the use of synonymous words.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Opposite lines
forms.about: The second line answers the first with its opposite.

defined.quote: This is when the words are contrasted in the two or more lines, being opposed in sense the one to the other.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Lines that build
forms.about: Each line is built the same way, or adds to the line before it.

defined.quote: This is where the parallelism consists only in the similar form of construction
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Mirror
forms.about: Words or lines go out in one order and come back in the reverse order.

defined.quote: This is when the parallel lines are so placed that if there be six lines, the first corresponds with the sixth, the second with the fifth, and the third with the fourth.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Lines that take turns
forms.about: The lines take turns: the first answers the third, and the second the fourth.

defined.quote: it is alternate when, of the four members, the first corresponds with the third, and the second with the fourth.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: One thing named for another
forms.about: One thing is named in place of another it goes with, such as a cause for its effect.

defined.quote: Metonymy is a figure by which one name or noun is used instead of another, to which it stands in a certain relation.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: A part for the whole
forms.about: A part is named for the whole, or the whole for a part.

forms.label: God in human terms
forms.about: Human feelings, actions or parts are spoken of God, so that we can understand Him.

defined.quote: This figure is used of the ascription of human passions, actions, or attributes to God.
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Things spoken of as persons
forms.about: Things or ideas are spoken of, or spoken to, as if they were persons.

defined.quote: A figure by which things are represented or spoken of as persons
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Like this
forms.about: One thing is said to be like another.

defined.quote: A Declaration that one Thing resembles another; or, Comparison by Resemblance
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: This is that
forms.about: One thing is said to be another, to show what it is like.

defined.quote: A Declaration that one Thing is (or represents) another; or, Comparison by Representation
defined.read: the UniqueBible.app module of the 1898 text, at github.com/darrelwright/UniqueBible_Books (commit 4017a67)

forms.label: Set side by side
forms.about: Two people are set side by side, and each shows up the other.

forms.label: Alike
forms.about: Two people are set side by side because one is like the other.
